item.text:
Continued. I varied which replica initiates recovery after the fast-chosen leader crashes. The recoverer matrix is informative:

- Recoverers 1 and 2 already hold the preaccepted chosen value; both preserve the chosen PUT on all four live replicas.
- Recoverers 3 and 4 have no local value; both follow the F1 NOOP path and commit NOOP on the live replicas.

```
recoverer=1: all live replicas keep the chosen PUT
recoverer=2: all live replicas keep the chosen PUT
recoverer=3: replicas 1-4 commit NOOP; crashed leader 0 keeps the PUT
recoverer=4: replicas 1-4 commit NOOP; crashed leader 0 keeps the PUT
```

This confirms the failure condition: a recoverer that lacks the value lets the synthetic local reply mask the preaccepted copies; a recoverer that already holds the value re-proposes it successfully. The all-alive partitioned-leader divergence remains the strongest result.
